title: New Startup Mindset: Ten Mindset Shifts to Build the Company of Your Dreams
author: Sandra Shpilberg
core_themes: Challenging traditional Silicon Valley startup myths
Developing a sustainable and founder-friendly company
Building a business on your own terms
primary_purpose: To guide readers through ten transformative mindset shifts that challenge the typical startup narrative, empowering them to build sustainable, fulfilling, and self-directed companies.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, encouraging, and personal; blends expert advice with storytelling
structure_format.organization: Ten chapters, each dedicated to a specific mindset shift, supported by case studies, anecdotes, and practical recommendations
features: Personal experiences from the author’s entrepreneurial journey

key_concepts_lessons: You don't need outside investment to succeed; bootstrapping is viable.
Defining success on your own terms leads to greater fulfillment.
Work-life balance and mental health matter as much as financial goals.
Rapid scaling and high-risk approaches aren’t the only paths to building a successful company.
Building and leading with authenticity fosters healthy company culture.
Resilience and adaptability are key entrepreneurial assets.
Startups can be built with intention, not just hustle and burnout.
notable_features: Combines practical guidance with introspective exercises
Addresses emotional and mental aspects of entrepreneurship
cultural_historical_context: Written in the late 2010s, the book echoes a growing movement questioning Silicon Valley’s venture-capital-driven growth models, and reflects increased awareness of sustainable, diverse, and inclusive entrepreneurship.
reception_impact: Well-received by aspiring founders and those disillusioned with mainstream startup narratives
Praised for practical, relatable advice and the author’s transparency
Noted as empowering especially for underrepresented groups in tech
Some critics suggest it may resonate more with solo founders or service-based businesses
comparable_titles: Company of One by Paul Jarvis
The Lean Startup by Eric Ries
Rework by Jason Fried and David Heinemeier Hansson
The Minimalist Entrepreneur by Sahil Lavingia
